findings.title: Imported feed HTML bypasses post sanitization
findings.body: This creates imported posts with `cook_method: raw_html`, so `Post#cook` stores the supplied HTML without the normal rendering and sanitization pipeline. RSS content is external input, and the polling code explicitly unescapes it; a feed publisher can therefore inject script-capable markup that is persisted and executed when users view the topic.

findings.title: Remote fetches can follow redirects to internal services
findings.body: `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects, but the embed URL is only checked against `embeddable_host` before this call. A URL on that host that redirects to a private or loopback address can make the server fetch internal resources; the response is then parsed and imported into a public topic, potentially exposing internal data.

findings.title: The Referer check can be forged to trigger imports
findings.body: A non-browser client can set an arbitrary `Referer` header, so this does not restrict requests to pages actually hosted on `embeddable_host`. Anyone can pass the check, request an uncached URL on that host, and cause `best` to enqueue a retrieval that may create a public topic. The per-URL throttle does not prevent abuse with distinct URLs.

findings.title: Description-only RSS items stop feed polling
findings.body: Standard RSS items commonly provide their body in `<description>`, not `<content>`. For an item without a `content` field, `i.content.scrub` raises instead of importing it; because the exception is not handled, it also prevents later items in the feed from being processed.

findings.title: Message origins are checked by substring rather than exact match
findings.body: This accepts any message origin that appears anywhere in `discourseUrl`, including a different origin that is a prefix of the configured forum hostname (for example, `https://forum.example.co` when the URL is `https://forum.example.com/`). Such a sender can post a `discourse-resize` message and manipulate the iframe height on the embedding page; compare parsed origins exactly.
